words.prose: {{ar:حَمَّالَةَ}} ({{tr:ḥammālata}}) turns the relational wife into a charged carrier-title. Its intensive feminine pattern makes carrying sound habitual and role-like, and its rarity inside a common carrying root makes the title feel specially selected rather than routine. The construct with {{ar:ٱلْحَطَبِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥaṭabi}}) compresses an action relation into a title without a finite verb. The accusative is not syntactically flat: it can mark state, appositional specification, or censure, and the censure reading lets the case ending itself participate in blame; by contrast, a nominative variant would make the epithet more directly predicate-like. The root's wider load-bearing field adds pressure from being made to bear, life-bearing, and burden-gear, while local grammar keeps fuel-carrying selected. The idiom keeps social harm present, and 111:3 keeps literal fuel in view; the doubled middle sound, the repeated rough onset with the fuel word, and the forward movement to 111:5 make the burden feel both audible and tightening.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَطَبِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥaṭabi}}) is the governed object that completes the carrier-title. Its genitive case binds it to {{ar:حَمَّالَةَ}} ({{tr:ḥammālata}}), while the definite article makes the phrase point to the firewood, not merely any fuel; an accusative-object variant would make the carrying more event-like, but the received genitive keeps the fuel annexed inside the title. The local fire in 111:3 selects literal combustible material first, but the root and idiom keep gathered harmful fuel, blind woodgathering, and social kindling in view, and the paired punishment-fuel occurrence at 72:15 gives the rare word a darker Quranic resonance. As the ayah's final word, it lands the scene on the material object: fuel heard as rough, specific, gathered, with the audible article boundary and clipped cadence placing it between the prior flame and the rope-material image of 111:5.

strongest_changes: The literal carrier becomes the logistical hinge in a name-to-flame circuit: the flame epithet is realized by the fuel she supplies.
Hands, wealth, acquisition, and ruin recast her work as the destructive counter-production of a failed household economy.
The tale-bearing branch and the feud branch allow social ignition and literal combustion to remain simultaneously active.
The neck, rope, and twisted cord reverse carrying gear onto the carrier, changing an agent who controls a load into a body bound and directed.
Generative branches for woman, pregnancy, fruit, flower, and fatherhood preserve an exploratory counter-fruition reading in which the household yields dead fuel.
summary.what_was_special: The focus is unusually compact but mechanically dense: person, intensive bearing, and fuel can organize literal labor, speech traffic, economic production, kinship, generativity, transport technology, and bodily reversal without forcing them into one final interpretation. Context repeatedly turns the carrier-cargo relation back on itself.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle how much syntactic force to assign to the marked relation between ٱمْرَأَتُهُ and حَمَّالَةَ, so the trace avoids making one grammatical parse decide the models.
The name-to-fate and household-economy arrows are reader-supplied causal organizations; lexical repetition alone does not prove those directions.
The counter-lineage, legal surety, bodily assimilation, and alimentary conduit readings depend on distant branch coexistence and must remain explicitly exploratory.
The rope may be the carrier's load gear reversed onto her, an independent restraint, an anti-ornament, a conjugal bond, or several of these at once; the packet does not disambiguate them.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The wife is an active fuel-supplier in the same mechanism as the fire.** Branch evidence: `م ر ء` B001, woman/person; `ح م ل` B001, bearing an outward load; `ح ط ب` B001, firewood gathered as fuel; earlier `ن و ر` B002, burning fire; `ل ه ب` B001, blazing flame. Structural cue: the fire of 111:3 is immediately followed by the woman carrying fuel. Assigned role: she supplies the logistical link between fire and combustible material. Abductive move: I infer that juxtaposition makes her carrying feed the preceding fire. Reading change: she is not a peripheral spouse; she becomes part of a supply chain that sustains the blaze.

2. **Carrying firewood also reads as carrying destructive speech.** Branch evidence: `ح ط ب` B003, carrying wood as tale-bearing and stirring harm; `ح ط ب` B002, night wood-gatherer mixing bad and good; earlier `ن و ر` B007, enmity flaring between people; `ك س ب` B001/B002, gain for self or brought to another. Structural cue: after wealth/earning and fire, the carrier appears with a noun whose branch explicitly includes slander and social ignition. Assigned role: firewood becomes speech-material that inflames relations. Abductive move: I supply that the carried object may be both literal fuel and socially combustible report. Reading change: the ayah reads as a portrait of participation in hostile circulation, not only physical labor.

3. **Inward bearing is inverted into destructive issue.** Branch evidence: `ح م ل` B002, pregnancy and inward bearing; `ر ح م` B003, womb; `ح ب ل` B006, pregnancy extending in the womb; `م ر ء` B001, woman; `ح ط ب` B001, fuel. Structural cue: a woman is named as a `حَمَّالَة`, while the packet opens with womb/kinship mercy and ends with a rope whose branches include pregnancy. Assigned role: carrying bridges fertility imagery and fuel imagery. Abductive move: I infer an inversion: the female capacity to bear inward life is overlaid by bearing outward fuel. Reading change: the phrase becomes an anti-gestation image, where what is borne issues in combustion rather than mercy or life.

4. **She bears liability rather than merely objects.** Branch evidence: `ح م ل` B003, bearing responsibility/sin; `ح م ل` B004, guarantee/indemnity; earlier `غ ن ي` B002, availing/replacing; `م و ل` B001, property; later `ح ب ل` B002, covenant/protection. Structural cue: wealth failed to avail in 111:2, and now a household member bears. Assigned role: carrying is moral/legal load-bearing, not just transport. Abductive move: I infer that after the failure of money as guarantee, the human carrier embodies the burden that cannot be transferred away. Reading change: she appears as co-bearer of obligation and harm, not as an incidental prop.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md:
- 111:5 immediately changed the wife-carrier image: the rope in her neck means the carrier is also carried, led, or constrained. `ح م ل` B001 and `ح ب ل` B001 therefore form a loop rather than a one-way action.
- The final `مَسَد` strengthened the material register of `حَطَب`. Twisting (`م س د` B001), binding (`ح ب ل` B001), and fuel (`ح ط ب` B001) make a coherent workshop of punishment: gathering, carrying, tying, and burning.
- The pregnancy branches were more surprising after the final ayah than during first reading. `ح م ل` B002, `ح ب ل` B006, and the opening `ر ح م` B003 create an anti-gestational counterimage: a woman bears not life but fuel/liability, and the cord is not hidden in the womb but exposed at the neck.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **An agent who supplies the preceding blaze.** **Lexical evidence:** `حَمَّالَة` has root `ح م ل`, branch `B001` (bearing an outward load), and `ٱلْحَطَب` has root `ح ط ب`, branch `B001` (firewood gathered, carried, or brought to another as fuel). `111:3` supplies `ص ل ي` branch `B004` (kindling and fuel) and `ل ه ب` branch `B001` (ignition). **Structure:** the conjunction introduces the wife directly after the man's fire sentence, and the intensive carrier noun is completed by the exact material that can sustain it. **Role and abduction:** load, fuel, and blaze are supplied; I infer that her repeated carrying enables the preceding fire's continuation. **Reading change:** the wife is not a passive relational appendage: the ayah assigns her an operational role in the fire mechanism.

2. **Speech-harm becomes a borne moral liability.** **Lexical evidence:** root `ح ط ب`, branch `B003`, treats carrying wood as tale-bearing, slander, and kindling harm; root `ح م ل`, branch `B003`, is responsibility, sin, trust, or moral burden. The preceding `نَار`, root `ن و ر`, branch `B007`, can denote enmity flaring among people. **Structure:** person (`ٱمْرَأَتُهُ`), intensive role (`حَمَّالَة`), and carried object (`ٱلْحَطَب`) form a complete agent-action-load construction after the social-fire possibility in `111:3`. **Role and abduction:** the packet supplies tale-bearing, burden, and enmity; I infer that carried reports cause hostility and return as the carrier's own liability. **Reading change:** the phrase diagnoses a social causal loop: she bears harmful speech outward and bears its responsibility inward.

3. **The collection tool rebounds onto the collector.** **Lexical evidence:** root `ح ط ب`, branch `B002`, images the night wood-gatherer who indiscriminately collects good and bad in a rope and may be harmed by it; `111:5` immediately supplies that `حَبْل`, root `ح ب ل`, branches `B001` (binding cord) and `B005` (entangling snare). Root `ح م ل`, branch `B006`, adds carrying gear or a strap. **Structure:** carrier and gathered wood are followed without an intervening scene by a cord on the carrier's own neck. **Role and abduction:** the packet itself supplies collection-in-a-rope and possible recoil; I infer that the same apparatus used to aggregate and transport the load becomes the means of restraint. **Reading change:** `حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَب` becomes a self-ensnaring practice, not just an occupational label.

4. **Familial bearing is inverted from generation to propagation of harm.** **Lexical evidence:** dormant root `ح م ل` branch `B002` covers pregnancy and inward fruit-bearing; `ٱمْرَأَتُهُ`, root `م ر ء`, branch `B001`, supplies the woman within a marriage relation. The opening root `ر ح م` branches `B002` (kinship) and `B003` (womb), and the final root `ح ب ل` branch `B006` (pregnancy extending in the womb), reinforce this generative field. **Structure:** instead of an inward life-bearing load, the intensive carrier bears dry fuel outward toward flame. **Role and abduction:** the packet supplies woman, kinship, womb, pregnancy, and outward fuel-bearing; I infer an inversion in which household generativity propagates combustion rather than life. **Reading change:** `حَمَّالَة` holds a dark counter-image to nurturing fertility: repeated bearing that multiplies destructive material.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `111:5` directly realizes the rope already embedded in `ح ط ب` branch `B002`'s night-gatherer image; its placement on her neck turns the gathering apparatus back upon the gatherer. The final `مَسَد` branch `B003` also adds duration, making `حَمَّالَة` sustained exertion rather than a static title. A weaker but newly visible bodily relation comes from root `م ر ء` branch `B004`: its `root_001409` variant is the esophagus near the throat, while its `root_001410` variant concerns eating or occasion-feeding; the later neck image and the carried fuel together invert feeding into supplying what the fire consumes.

findings.text: Kadın, önceki alevin kenarında duran bir eş değil, taşıdığı odunla onu besleyen etkin tedarikçi olarak görünür.
Odun, zarar verici söz ve dedikodu olarak da işler: taşıdığı şey düşmanlığı dışarıda körüklerken sorumluluğu kendi üzerine yükler.
Kadın ve taşıma görüntüsü, içeride yaşam büyüten taşımayı tersine çevirir; burada dışarı taşınan yük yaşamı değil ateşi çoğaltır.
Malın güvence olamadığı yerde onun taşıması, borcu başkasından uzaklaştıran bir kefalet değil, paylaşılan ve devredilemeyen bir sorumluluk olur.
Toplama ve taşıma aracı, sonraki boyun bağıyla taşıyanın kendisini yakalayan bir düzene dönüşür.
Son ipin süreklilik çağrışımı, taşıyıcılığı tek seferlik bir işten çıkarıp tekrarlanan, yorucu bir uğraşa dönüştürür.
Sonraki boyun görüntüsü, ateşi beslemek üzere taşınan yük ile taşıyanın boğazından bağlanması arasında bedensel bir tersine dönüş kurar.

facets.statement: Yakılmaya hazırlanan odun, dal ve benzeri bitkisel parçalar yakacak olarak adlandırılır.
Bu yakacağı arayıp bir araya getirme eylemi dalın temel süreç anlamıdır.
Odun, kişinin kendisi yerine bir başkası için toplanabilir veya o kişiye getirilebilir.
Belirli bir yer, orada çok miktarda odun bulunması bakımından nitelenebilir.
Belirli bir niteleme, kuru diken veya odun yiyen dişi deveyi anlatır.
Bağın üst dallarının odun olarak kesilecek duruma gelmesi ve kesilen odunluk dallar, bağcılığa özgü kullanımlardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, yakacak odunu ve onu toplamayı merkezde tutar; başkası için toplama, odunca zengin yer, kuru bitki yiyen dişi deve ve bağdan kesilen odunluk dallar bu merkezin özel kullanımlarıdır.
